clue.text: Admits dresses lack glamour at first sight

indicators.note: the dresses lack a letter, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: gowns are dresses

indicators.note: what is seen first of glamour is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a set of frocks looks drab when first seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess or acknowledge it.

clue.text: Test, say, item from teetotaller's menu

definitions.meaning: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, an example of a stream or channel of flowing water
read playfully, a meal course for someone who drinks nothing stronger than water

explanation.surface: An exam is compared to a dish on the menu of someone who never drinks alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Test is an example of a natural channel through which a stream flows.

clue.text: Rugby forwards in another fracas

parts.note: a second helping is another one
a row is a noisy quarrel or fracas

explanation.surface: Rugby forwards get involved in yet another brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the locks packing behind the front three of the scrum form this forward line.

clue.text: Warning athlete there's one coming ahead

parts.note: golfers shout this word to warn of a ball heading towards someone
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a warning that an athlete is approaching from in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A precursor or herald is someone who goes before and signals what follows.

clue.text: Start to feel a pain, not eating

indicators.note: the start of the word feel is its opening letter

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone begins to feel a pang of hunger while going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from food, as during a religious observance, means going without eating.

clue.text: Whips support so-called rule with rec scoundrels and come down hard

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Whips support so-called rule with rec scoundrels and come down hard', is garbled: CATS (whips) + RAIN (sounds like reign, rule) + AND + DOGS (scoundrels) fits, but 'support' and 'with rec' have no job and the order is scrambled
annotationWithheld.clue: Whips support so-called rule with rec scoundrels and come down hard

clue.text: Outstanding work from vicar — love story accepted

indicators.note: the vicar's title accepts, or takes in, the story

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar
a lie is a false story
love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clergyman's romantic tale is taken in by readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is literal: the work stands out from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is sculpture in relief, a work in which the figures project from the surface.

clue.text: Old name but new sign

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: An ancient name is said to be a fresh portent.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the family name, such as Julius, was the gens name, the second of a citizen's names.

clue.text: Remove soap from water in sewer

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Getting the soap off with water in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'wateR IN SEwer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash out soapy suds with clean water is to swill them away.

clue.text: Shares even now not moving at all

parts.note: stocks are shares in companies
still means even now, as in 'it is still raining'

explanation.surface: Share prices are, even now, completely static.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely motionless, like an animal frozen in place, is the idiom meant.

clue.text: The sweet wine is capital here

definitions.text: The sweet wine is capital here

parts.words: The sweet wine is capital here
parts.note: muscat is a sweet wine, and Muscat is also the capital city of a Gulf state

explanation.surface: Someone praises a dessert wine as excellent in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to mean splendid; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat, sharing its name with a sweet wine, is the capital of this Arabian sultanate.

clue.text: Turbine without a starter is crazy for sultanate

indicators.note: the remaining letters go crazy and are rearranged
the word loses its first letter, its starter

explanation.surface: A turbine that will not start up is behaving madly in a small kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a starter' drops T, leaving URBINE, and 'is crazy' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich state on Borneo ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Sort of table that creates confidence

definitions.meaning: a ... table is a small side table in a church holding the bread and wine
belief or trust, as in giving weight to a report

explanation.surface: A kind of table is said to inspire trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A credence table holds the Eucharist elements; the word also means belief or trust in something.

clue.text: Constable print gets a good hand

parts.note: a police constable is a copper
a plate is a printed illustration in a book

explanation.surface: A painting by the English artist John Constable earns praise as a fine piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests the painter; it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copperplate is a neat, flowing style of handwriting, so a good hand in penmanship.

clue.text: Inadequate publicity about spectacles

indicators.note: the publicity goes about, or around, the spectacles

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
OO looks like a pair of round glasses

explanation.surface: Weak advertising surrounds a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of low quality or insufficient is inadequate, a common synonym.

clue.text: Approach purposefully and reach the luggage

definitions.meaning: to tackle a problem firmly and decisively
a grip is a travel bag, so arriving at the bags

explanation.surface: Someone strides with determination to collect the suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deal firmly with something; literally it can mean reaching the holdalls.

clue.text: Concerned with people giving information revealing country's means of defence

parts.note: re means concerning or about
sources are people who supply information, especially to journalists

explanation.surface: Informants reveal a nation's defence capabilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's resources are its stock of assets and means, which it can call on to defend itself.

clue.text: Long Western shot through thick old lens

indicators.note: the scrambled letters run through the middle of the word for thick

parts.note: crass means stupid or thick

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A long cowboy film shot through a heavy antique lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges LONG and W to OWNGL, which goes 'through' CRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown glass is an old hand-blown glass, still used for optical lenses.

clue.text: Unhurried response

definitions.meaning: slow and steady, happening by degrees
in church, an antiphon sung between the Epistle and Gospel at Mass

explanation.surface: A slow reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual means step by step; in the liturgy it is a sung response after the Epistle.

clue.text: Cracking clues following a struggle

indicators.note: cracking breaks the word apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for 'and the following pages'

explanation.surface: Solving the clues follows a hard struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like solving the clues; it rearranges CLUES with FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle is a brief, confused fight or tussle.

clue.text: Visionary's derisive smile, name-dropping

definitions.note: read as 'visionary is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the word drops the letter for name

parts.note: a sneer is a scornful smile

explanation.surface: A prophet sneers at people who drop famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name-dropping' looks like boasting of famous acquaintances; it says drop N.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet, someone with visions of the future.

clue.text: Wake in this place — a hospital room

parts.note: here means in this place
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone wakes up here, in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake was an English rebel against William the Conqueror; 'Wake' is his epithet, not waking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward, the eleventh-century outlaw of the Fens, was nicknamed the Wake.

clue.text: Bible circle in church set-up is in disorder

indicators.note: the Bible and circle go in the church
in a down clue, set up means turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A Bible study circle in a church organisation is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns CH to HC, and AVO goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc means widespread chaos or confusion.

clue.text: Desert with a new kind of palm tree

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: An arid place with a fresh sort of palm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratan (rattan) is a climbing palm whose stems are used for cane furniture.

clue.text: USSR, up to trouble, takes over

indicators.note: the letters are troubled, or stirred up, into a new order

explanation.surface: The Soviet Union, looking for trouble, seizes power.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a throne or power wrongfully, taking it over.

clue.text: Stop doctor taking oxygen

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A physician is barred from taking oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a ban that stops a proposal going ahead.

clue.text: Secretary-General, say, off the record

definitions.meaning: the Secretary-General is an example of a United Nations official

explanation.surface: A top diplomat speaks without attribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a UN functionary; as one, it means not formally sanctioned.

clue.text: Improve combine to bring in new harvest centrally

indicators.note: the word for combine brings the other letters inside it

parts.note: to coalesce is to combine into one

indicators.note: the central letter of harvest is taken

explanation.surface: A farmer upgrades the combine harvester to gather a new crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' and 'harvest' suggest farm machinery; combine is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to recover health, so to improve after illness.

clue.text: Separate shelter

definitions.meaning: to cast off or part from, as a tree drops its leaves
a hut or outbuilding used for storage or cover

explanation.surface: A detached hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off; a shed is also a simple outbuilding giving shelter.
